customize.text: Sanhaj Kompore

Sanhaj Kompore was one of the six heroes of Natlan, a great high priest and a Border Master of the Masters of the Night-Wind, who lived over five hundred years ago. As a child, Sanhaj was mute, his consciousness clouded, and the Mictlan elder who tended the tribe's sacrificial fire said that half of the boy's soul was lost in the night flames. On his birthday, the silent child stepped into the barren stone lands to find the missing self. His soul had to cross seven curtain layers to gain an audience with the Lord of the Night. The only Iktomisaurus who agreed to accompany the boy into unknown lands was Mahamba. In the long hall paved with obsidian, Sanhaj felt like a person whose eyes were opened for the first time. Ancient realms flowed like water through his pupils, the first Pyro Archon made a vow to his forces, and the tyrant of the Cinder City was overthrown by a crimson-eyed youth. After experiencing the past, the boy understood all words, their syllabic structures, and their meanings, and he saw the depths of the skeins of time. He saw a
that would soon cover the whole of Natlan and the monsters from
He saw a lonely isle and a
burrowing at all boundaries like a tarsal maggot, ravaging like a fire. Where the black shadow lay, the dead and those yet to die wept aloud. When the dark fog was about to touch the tribes of Natlan, the boy could not help but cry, <color=#ffffffd9>"Stop!"</color> Suddenly, he awoke and found himself lying near a blue bonfire, and an elder was handing him a ceremonial staff.

From that day on, Sanhaj became the great storyteller of the Masters of the Night-Wind. He censured the fools who ignored the dangers of the future and began to weave a great net of lies to hide a past that should never be touched again. Sanhaj Kompore received the Ancient Name
likely borne by the hero
He fought alongside the first Pyro Archon and, during the reign of the tyrant of the Cinder City, founded the Mictlan tribe in the valley. Five hundred years after Sanhaj's death, the Ancient Name Bidii was inherited by one of the six heroes of Natlan, Ororon.

<color=#ffffffd9>"My Ancient Name... 'Bidii.'</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>It means "devotion." You will give your all not for the sake of a heroic death, but to do justice by the answer you've found for your life.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>For that answer, you will offer all of your strength, and be born anew. Through your devotion, you will prove your worth.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>'Having foretold his own death, the omniscient man holds a feast in celebration.'</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>'Let us raise our cups in honor of his heroism and send him off with this final tribute.'</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>'For, at last, his wish is now fulfilled.'"</color>

In the net of deceit, Sanhaj told countless stories and jokes, tinged with the moonlit darkness. One of the stories he told, disbelieved by his tribesmen, was about himself. Long ago, there was a cunning rogue amongst the Masters of the Night-Wind named Kompore. He was skilled in deception and theft, gaining advantage by both cunning and force, and thus was notorious within the tribe, but he had an honest brother named Sanhaj. At that time, the Lord of the Crossroads still walked among mortals, guiding them to the netherworld and merging their souls into the great black river. It is said that at the end of the black river, he built a brewery, where he could reveal the fate of any person in dreams by drinking the mushroom wine brewed there. Kompore the Cunning decided that if he had such a gift, he could become like the tribe's prophets, who predict fate and reveal the truth. His rogue's eyes roved about, imagining the profits this secret knowledge would bring him.

To trick the Lord of the Crossroads out of this miraculous mushroom wine, Kompore went to his honest brother, Sanhaj, and made him promise to keep his treacherous plan a secret. He offered his brother to go to the Lord of the Crossroads and tell him that he was terminally ill, and that Sanhaj needed Papa Witch Doctor's medicine, which would heal Kompore. While Sanhaj and the Lord of the Crossroads conversed, Kompore would sneak into the brewery and steal the mushroom wine. The kind Sanhaj wanted to refuse, but he had already agreed to the first request, so he was forced to comply. Tormented by guilt, Sanhaj revealed his brother's plan to the Lord of the Crossroads, and Mama Dream-Realm embraced him and kissed his forehead. But at that moment, Kompore burst into his sleeping brother's tent and threw a rough hemp rope around his neck. He knew in advance that Sanhaj would reveal his plan to the Lord of the Crossroads. And so, before the master of dreams could even issue a warning, Sanhaj met his end at the hands of his own brother. The obsidian cup filled with mushroom wine slipped from his grasp, staining his chest and the blood-soaked hemp rope tightly wound around his neck.
The Lord of the Crossroads was enraged by Sanhaj's death and cursed Kompore: his unhappy brother Sanhaj would be resurrected within him, and would prophesize the fullness of his fate. From that moment on, all those he had deceived and murdered would be forever etched in his memory, and every lie he had ever told, his brother would repeat a thousand times over in his ear. From then on, he was known by a new name: Sanhaj Kompore. And only when the exiled hero called him to battle against the black shadow was he able to atone for his sins.

customize.text: The Cataclysm

When the Cataclysm struck five hundred years ago, and a black wave engulfed Natlan, Sanhaj knew he was destined to perish in the battle with the black shadow he had foreseen as a child. The exiled hero Tenoch was the first to unite the warring tribes and stand against the monsters of the Abyss. And although Sanhaj knew of their heroic end in what would later be called the Mare Jivari, he and his companion Mahamba joined Tenoch.
<color=#ffffffd9>"But nay, it matters little, it matters not! Perhaps there may come a day when the scoundrel made famous for being clever as a viper shall become a hero."</color>

Sanhaj Kompore was more than just a trickster and storyteller; he was also Mictlan's greatest Border Master. "Border Master" is an honorific title bestowed only upon exceptional individuals, and the most powerful among them can expand the boundaries of the Night Kingdom, allowing a part of it to temporarily manifest in the real world. To perform rituals, blurring the boundary between the Night Kingdom and the present world, Sanhaj forged a ceremonial blade named "Calamity of Eshu." Of all the Abyssal monsters that had attacked Natlan five hundred years ago, the most terrifying was Bakunawa, the creation of the Khaenri'ahn alchemist, Rhinedottir. It destroyed entire settlements on the island of Tenochtzitoc until only a single survivor, Tenoch, remained. The monster was impossible to kill: even when it was beheaded or had its body chopped into pieces, the remains would somehow continue to grow, seeking each other out and eventually, forming a new, revitalized Bakunawa. Realizing that Bakunawa could consume all of Natlan, Tenoch and Sanhaj chose to sacrifice themselves. The exiled hero let the Border Master perform Phlogiston Engraving on his body in order to unleash the power of border spells to expand the boundaries of the Night Kingdom and manifest a portion of it in the real world. Then, Tenoch allowed himself to be eaten by Bakunawa. With Tenoch's body as the ritual offering, Sanhaj summoned a miniature Night Kingdom inside Bakunawa's belly, and the clash between the powers of the Abyss, the Lord of the Night, and Tenoch's spirit in Bakunawa's body led to a violent explosion that shattered the monster into innumerable pieces. The explosion created the Mare Jivari, and the leader of the united army of the Natlan tribes and the Border Master perished.

After the Cataclysm, Sanhaj's apprentice's apprentice, the shaman Liriwu, set out with a group of travelers to Ochkanatlan to retrieve the Jade of Return, a legendary artifact capable of destroying the Abyss forever. But in Ochkanatlan, they were met not by the Jade of Return, but by a dragon and the Abyssal monsters. As a result, the entire group perished, and only Liriwu survived and returned to Natlan to seek help. Five hundred years later, the great shaman's heir is Conulaf, a trainee priestess who constantly finds herself in trouble. According to her, the elders told her that her ancestor, Sanhaj, often bet against people from other tribes and cheated them: <color=#ffffffd9>"Go make and win some bets! That's the only way to qualify as a true Master of the Night-Wind!"</color> Conulaf saw a competition between the saurians and bet on the Iktomisaurus, but it lost, and the woman ended up locked in a cage.

Five hundred years later, when Natlan faced the final battle against the Abyss, Sanhaj's spirit, along with five other Natlan heroes who bore the Ancient Names of the first Pyro Archon's companions, assisted his successor, Ororon, in empowering the current Archon to destroy the Abyss. Moreover, the fragments of Sanhaj's bow, even after five hundred years, did not lose their power and were used to open a passage to the Mare Jivari, where the immortal Bakunawa was sealed. To battle Bakunawa, the great shaman Citlali used the "Calamity of Eshu," which contains the power of the Wayob. With this same blade, Citlali was able to save the soul of a man lost in the Night Kingdom.

customize.name: Shuttle of Odara
customize.desc:
Specialized refinement material for "Calamity of Eshu."
Refracting an eerie, prism-like light, this jade pendant emits a chilling aura that does not disappear, even were it to be cast within a roaring blaze.
In ancient shamanic traditions, the "shuttle" symbolizes a medium that pierces through different realms. It is said that in the era of barbarism, before humans knew how to count their days or to weave their tales, the mighty dragons who then roamed the Soulfire Plains had a word for a construct that traversed the pitch-black darkness between the stars. In their long-forgotten language, they called such creations "Void Shuttles" — blazing javelins that could pierce anything, even a veil thick enough to enshroud an entire world.
Of course, given that the source of this story was the crafty trickster Sanhaj, it may well be that this was nothing but another of his countless tall tales, told with the sole intention of earning himself a meal and a drink. Today, some of the most respected priests of the Masters of the Night-Wind still hold this view.
